newsitem.title: POLAND: POLIFARB-C TRADE UNIONS THREATEN STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: POLIFARB-C TRADE UNIONS THREATEN STRIKE.

text.p: Workers of Polish paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn SA, protesting against terms of the firm's planned merger with Polifarb Wroclaw SA, gave the management a deadline until Monday to respond to their demands.

The unions, which declared strike alert on Wednesday, will hold a referenum on February 18 on whether to go on full strike, unless their demands are met, local Solidarity head Jerzy Pieczonka said on Thursday.
Solidarity and other unions in Polifarb Cieszyn do not reject the merger but are protesting against plans to set the merged company's headquarters in Wroclaw.
"As far as the merger, which we do not reject, is concerned -- we fight for Cieszyn to be the company's headquarters...the management has time until Monday to reply," Pieczonka told Reuters.
Polifarb Cieszyn's president Bernard Andrzejewski said negotiations with the trade unions were underway, adding he hoped the unions would decide not to go on strike.
"I do not think the employees would like to act against themselves and I hope there will be no strike," he told Reuters.
After the planned merger, likely to take place in July, analysts expect the two firms to command about 40 percent of Poland's paint market.
